documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

31F here to establish. Prior PCP records reviewed (see Media).

HTN: told she had high BP around 2020 on several office checks, before her first baby. Put on labetalol during that pregnancy and simply stayed on it - 200 mg BID. Takes it with breakfast and dinner, rarely misses. No home cuff. No headaches, chest pain, visual change. She and her husband would like a second child in the next year or so, which is why the prior office left her on labetalol. Already taking a prenatal vitamin daily.

PMH: HTN. Lots of ear infections as a kid, tubes in both ears; no ear trouble as an adult.
PSH: tympanostomy tubes (childhood). OB: G1P1, SVD 2021 at term, no complications she knows of.
Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID; prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother and father both with high blood pressure.
SH: preschool/daycare teacher (toddler room). Smoked in her late teens and early 20s, roughly 5 pack-years, stopped at 26. No alcohol. No drugs. Married, one child.

ROS: negative except as above.

Exam: BP and HR as charted, at goal on labetalol. Well-appearing. HEENT: TMs intact bilaterally with some old tube scarring, canals clear. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear to auscultation throughout. Abd soft. No LE edema. Skin warm.

A/P
1. Chronic hypertension - controlled on labetalol 200 BID. Reasonable agent given pregnancy plans; continue. Discussed home BP cuff. Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, UA.
2. Preconception - continue prenatal vitamin. Asked her to message us when pregnant so we can get her to OB early.
3. Health maintenance: Pap/HPV 2021 normal, next due 2026. HIV and hep C screening offered, accepted. Flu and COVID this autumn at a nurse visit. PHQ-2 0.

RTC 6 months for BP.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wendy - everything from last week came back fine: kidney function, potassium, blood counts, cholesterol and urine all normal, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Keep up the labetalol and we'll check in again in the new year.

documents.title: RE: Pregnant!
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! By your dates you're due around September 18. No need to come here first. I've sent a referral to your OB group so they can see you early, since your blood pressure makes this a pregnancy they'll want to follow closely. Keep taking the labetalol 200 mg twice a day and the prenatal vitamin - labetalol is one of the preferred blood pressure medicines in pregnancy. Call us or them if you get a severe headache, vision changes, or readings of 160/110 or more.

Maternal care for known or suspected poor fetal growth, third trimester

reports.study: Obstetric ultrasound, fetal growth with umbilical artery velocimetry
reports.text: Single live intrauterine pregnancy, cephalic. Gestational age by early dating 28w0d. Fetal biometry: estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile for gestational age. Amniotic fluid index within normal limits. Placenta posterior, no previa. Umbilical artery waveform: increased resistance with elevated systolic/diastolic ratio for gestational age; end-diastolic flow present. Fetal heart rate normal. Survey of visualized anatomy unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile with elevated umbilical artery S/D ratio, consistent with fetal growth restriction. Normal amniotic fluid. Recommend serial growth and umbilical artery surveillance.

documents.title: Obstetrics prenatal visit, 28 weeks
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside Obstetrics & Gynecology - prenatal visit
Date of service: 06/26/2024

Dear Doctor,

I saw your patient Wendy Lavoie today, 32 years old, G2P1, at 28w0d by early dating.

Her chronic hypertension remains well controlled on labetalol 200 mg twice daily. She takes it and her prenatal vitamin faithfully. Her first child was born at term without complications. No tobacco, alcohol or drugs. No headache, visual change or RUQ pain. Allergies: NKDA.

BP 138/86. Examination unremarkable; fundal height noted.

Growth ultrasound today shows an estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile, a normal amniotic fluid index, and increased umbilical artery resistance with an elevated S/D ratio, with end-diastolic flow present.

Impression:
1. Chronic hypertension in pregnancy, controlled on labetalol.
2. Fetal growth restriction with abnormal umbilical artery indices.

Plan: continue labetalol 200 mg BID and prenatal vitamin. Serial growth scans with umbilical artery studies and antenatal testing; we will plan delivery at 37 weeks if surveillance stays reassuring, sooner if not. Tdap given today. Preeclampsia precautions reviewed.

Thank you for sharing her care.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

Hospital Labor & Delivery - Discharge Summary
Admitted 08/28/2024  Discharged 08/30/2024

Admission diagnosis: intrauterine pregnancy at 37w0d; fetal growth restriction with elevated umbilical artery S/D ratio; chronic hypertension on labetalol.

Course: Admitted for planned induction at 37 weeks following serial surveillance. Labor induced. Uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery the evening of 08/28 of a liveborn female, 2,410 g, small for gestational age, vigorous at birth, to the newborn nursery. Estimated blood loss within normal range. Blood pressures remained controlled on her home labetalol 200 mg twice daily throughout; no features of preeclampsia. Breastfeeding established.

Discharge diagnoses: SVD at 37w0d, G2P2; chronic hypertension, controlled.
Discharge medications: labetalol 200 mg PO BID; prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: postpartum visit with obstetrics in 6 weeks; BP check with PCP after that; home BP log meanwhile.

documents.title: Postpartum call

No headache, vision change, SOB or leg swelling. Bleeding tapering. Mood ok, tired. OB postpartum appt 10/9. Asked her to book a BP visit with us for later in October; she will bring her log.

orders.reason: chronic foul right otorrhea with hearing loss

documents.title: Office Visit - R ear
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: right ear draining.

HPI: Since about July the right ear has leaked on and off - yellowish, and she says the smell is strong enough that others notice. No pain to speak of. Hearing on that side has slowly gone down; she now turns her left ear toward people and has trouble in a loud room. Denies spinning or ringing. No fever. No swimming. Had tubes as a child and many infections then, none since her early teens.

Meds: labetalol 200 BID, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. R ear: moist debris and discharge in the canal, could not see the drum well after gentle cleaning. L ear: canal clear, TM intact. No mastoid tenderness or swelling. No facial asymmetry. Neck without nodes.

A/P: Chronic right otorrhea with progressive hearing loss in a patient with a childhood tube history. Five months of foul drainage needs an ENT look under the microscope rather than another round of drops from me. Referral placed; front desk to request the earliest opening. Keep the ear dry (cotton ball with petroleum jelly in the shower). Return sooner for pain, swelling behind the ear, dizziness or facial weakness.

conditions.label: Conductive hearing loss, unilateral, right ear, with unrestricted hearing on the contralateral side

medications.sig: Instill 5 drops in the right ear twice daily for 10 days

reports.text: Pure-tone air and bone conduction, both ears. Right: conductive hearing loss, average air-bone gap 30 dB across the speech frequencies; bone conduction thresholds within normal limits. Word recognition 96% at comfortable level. Left: hearing within normal limits, word recognition 100%. Tympanometry deferred on the right because of drainage; left type A.
reports.conclusion: Right conductive hearing loss, average air-bone gap 30 dB. Normal left ear.

documents.title: Otolaryngology consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside Otolaryngology - Head & Neck Surgery
Date of service: 01/06/2025
Referred by: primary care, for right otorrhea

History: 32-year-old woman with chronic hypertension, four months postpartum (seen by obstetrics through her pregnancy last year), with half a year of right ear drainage that is frequently malodorous, plus steadily declining hearing on the right. Background noise is the hardest part; group conversation at work is a strain. No vertigo, no tinnitus. Many ear infections in childhood with bilateral tubes, but nothing in the last twenty years.

Medications: labetalol 200 mg twice daily; prenatal vitamin daily. Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Social: daycare teacher; former smoker, about 5 pack-years, quit at 26; no alcohol.
Family: both parents hypertensive.

Examination under the microscope: Right - after suctioning of the canal, the tympanic membrane is intact but retracted, with a pearly white mass in the superior quadrant at the attic. Left - normal canal and drum. Tuning forks: conductive pattern on the right. Facial nerve intact bilaterally. Nose, oral cavity, oropharynx and neck normal.

Audiogram today: right conductive loss, average air-bone gap 30 dB, word recognition 96%; left normal.

Impression: Right attic cholesteatoma with conductive hearing loss.

Plan:
- Ofloxacin otic, 5 drops right ear twice daily for 10 days; strict water precautions.
- CT temporal bones without contrast for surgical planning.
- Surgery is the treatment. We discussed right tympanomastoidectomy, its goal of a safe dry ear, and the possibility of a later look for residual disease. She would like to proceed once the ear is drier.

Thank you for the referral.
Otolaryngology

reports.text:
Temporal bone protocol. Technique: axial thin-section images of both temporal bones without contrast, with coronal reformats.
Right: soft-tissue mass in the epitympanum with blunting of the scutum. Ossicular chain intact. Tegmen tympani and lateral semicircular canal intact. Facial nerve canal intact. The mastoid air cells are otherwise aerated. External auditory canal clear.
Left: middle ear and mastoid clear and well aerated. Ossicles normal.
Inner ear structures normal bilaterally. Visualized brain unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Right epitympanic soft-tissue mass with scutal blunting, consistent with cholesteatoma. No erosion of the ossicles, tegmen or lateral semicircular canal. Normal left temporal bone.

documents.title: Pre-op evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-operative H&P for R tympanomastoidectomy 3/12 (ENT, general anesthesia, outpatient). ENT letter and CT reviewed - right attic cholesteatoma.

Feels well. Finished the ear drops, drainage much less. Climbs two flights carrying a toddler without chest pain or breathlessness. No personal or family problems with anesthesia. No bleeding history. Not pregnant; still nursing at night. Back at work.

Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: BP at goal, vitals otherwise normal. Airway: normal mouth opening, good dentition. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

Assessment: low-risk patient for a low-risk procedure. No testing needed beyond what ENT requires. Take labetalol with a sip of water the morning of surgery. Cleared - letter faxed to ENT surgical scheduler.

reports.text:
Specimen: right middle ear and attic, cholesteatoma matrix.
Gross: multiple fragments of tan-white flaky tissue.
Microscopic: keratinizing stratified squamous epithelium with abundant laminated keratin debris and underlying fibrous tissue. No dysplasia or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Right middle ear and attic: cholesteatoma (keratinizing squamous epithelium with keratin debris). Negative for malignancy.

documents.title: Operative report - right tympanomastoidectomy
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside Otolaryngology - Ambulatory Surgery Center
Date of surgery: 03/12/2025

Preoperative / postoperative diagnosis: right attic cholesteatoma.
Procedure: right canal-wall-up tympanomastoidectomy with tympanic membrane reconstruction (temporalis fascia).
Anesthesia: general. Facial nerve monitoring used throughout.

Findings: cholesteatoma in the attic. Ossicular chain intact and preserved. Facial nerve canal, tegmen and lateral canal intact. Matrix removed completely under the microscope.

EBL minimal. No complications. Discharged home the same afternoon in stable condition, facial function normal.

Plan: dry ear precautions, packing to stay in place until the post-op visit in six weeks; diffusion-weighted MRI at one year to look for residual disease. Pathology to follow.
Otolaryngology

documents.title: Ear surgery went fine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just letting you know the ear surgery was last Wednesday and went well. Ear is packed and a little achy but no fever. The surgeon said it all came out. No questions, just wanted you to have the update!

documents.title: RE: Ear surgery went fine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update, glad it went smoothly. Their report and the pathology just came in and confirm what they told you. Keep it dry and follow their instructions for the packing.

documents.title: Otolaryngology post-operative visit
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside Otolaryngology
Date of service: 04/23/2025

Six weeks after right canal-wall-up tympanomastoidectomy. Packing removed. Postauricular incision well healed. Graft intact and healing, ear dry. Facial function normal. She thinks her hearing is about where it was before surgery.

Pathology confirmed cholesteatoma.

Plan: may resume getting the ear wet in two more weeks. Non-echo-planar diffusion-weighted MRI next spring, about a year after surgery, to screen for residual disease. Sooner for drainage or pain.
Otolaryngology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL - 33F

Interval: daughter delivered 8/2024 at 37 wk (FGR). R attic cholesteatoma removed 3/2025 (canal-wall-up tympanomastoidectomy), healing well per ENT; MRI planned spring 2026. Weaned from nursing in May.

Concerns today: since the winter she brings up phlegm most mornings and every cold from the toddler room seems to leave a cough for weeks. No fever, no blood, no weight concern raised. She shrugs it off as the daycare.

Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID; prenatal vitamin (asked about stopping; fine either way, she prefers to keep it). NKDA.
SH: former smoker, quit at 26. No alcohol.

Exam: BP at goal, vitals as charted. Weight down to 69.5 kg from 73.5 last fall, postpartum. HEENT: R ear healed postauricular incision, canal dry; L TM normal. Neck no nodes or thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout, no wheeze or crackles. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin no rashes. Ext no edema.

A/P
1. Chronic HTN - controlled. Continue labetalol 200 BID. CMP today.
2. Morning phlegm / post-cold cough - likely postviral with constant exposures at work; lungs clear. Return if it changes, if blood, fever, or weight loss.
3. Cholesteatoma s/p surgery - ENT following.
4. HM - CBC, CMP, lipids. Pap/HPV due 2026. Vaccines up to date for the season; flu and COVID in the fall. PHQ-2 0.

Follow up 6 months or as needed.

documents.title: Lab results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Wendy, your results are all within the normal range - blood counts, kidneys, liver, sugar and cholesterol. Nothing to do. Enjoy the summer.

documents.body: Hi, I'm leaving September 8 for a two-month volunteer program overseas (rural area, back early November). Could I get enough labetalol to cover the whole time plus some extra? My pharmacy says insurance needs a vacation override.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Consolidation in the right lower lobe. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Left lung clear. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contours normal. Bones unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Right lower lobe consolidation, consistent with pneumonia.

documents.title: Sick visit - cough, fever
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Same-day visit (texted this morning).

S: Got home Nov 7 from two months volunteering in a rural area abroad. About 4 days ago fever up to 38.6 at home and her usual morning phlegm turned into a much heavier cough with thick yellow-green sputum through the day. No blood. Tired. No known sick contacts on the flights. No leg swelling.

Meds: labetalol 200 BID, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

O: SpO2 96% RA, other vitals as charted; weight 67.0. Mildly ill-appearing, speaking full sentences. Crackles at the right base, no wheeze; left clear. Heart regular. No calf tenderness.
CXR (read same day): right lower lobe consolidation.
CBC: WBC 13.6.

A/P: Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe, fine for outpatient treatment. Doxycycline 100 mg BID x 7 days. Fluids, rest. Recheck in 2 weeks; sooner for worsening breathing, persistent fever past 72 hours on treatment, or chest pain. Travel history noted - if symptoms don't fully settle we'll think more broadly.

documents.title: Follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt day 2 of doxycycline. Fever lower overnight than before. Taking with food and water, staying upright after doses. Breathing ok, no worse. Reminded of 12/3 recheck. Will call sooner if fever persists past the weekend.

orders.reason: persistent purulent sputum with blood streaks and weight loss after right lower lobe pneumonia

documents.title: Follow-up - pneumonia
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Fever broke after 3 days on doxycycline and has not come back; finished the course. But the sputum hasn't gone away: every day, thick and yellow-green, worst first thing in the morning - she fills tissues before breakfast - and it smells bad. A few times there have been streaks of blood mixed in. More tired than she'd expect, winded on stairs carrying her daughter. Looking back, the morning phlegm has been there since last winter.

Weight: 66.4 today vs 69.5 at the June physical, without trying.

O: Afebrile, SpO2 normal on RA. Coarse crackles persist at the right base. Heart regular. No nodes in the neck or axillae.

A/P
1. Persistent purulent sputum with blood streaking and weight loss after RLL pneumonia; recent two months in a high-TB-incidence region; daycare exposure. This needs a chest specialist. Pulmonology referral placed, urgent slot requested. Quantiferon today. Mask at work until we hear back on TB testing.
2. Pneumonia - fever resolved; closing as treated.
3. Weight loss - 3 kg since June, unintended. Tracking.
4. Flu and COVID given today (missed the fall while away).
5. HTN - BP fine on labetalol.

documents.title: TB blood test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your TB blood test (Quantiferon) is negative. That's reassuring, though it doesn't settle everything by itself, so the lung specialist may still want sputum samples. You can stop masking at work. Pulmonology has you for January 5.

events.reason: chronic productive cough, hemoptysis, weight loss

medications.drug: amoxicillin 875 MG / clavulanate 125 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food for 14 days

results.text: Normal oropharyngeal flora. No predominant pathogen isolated.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Parallel linear densities and ring shadows at the right lung base, in keeping with thickened, dilated bronchi. No consolidation. No cavity or mass. No pleural effusion. Left lung clear. Heart and mediastinum normal.
reports.conclusion: Tram-track and ring opacities at the right base suggesting bronchiectasis. Prior right lower lobe consolidation has cleared.

documents.title: Pulmonary Medicine consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside Pulmonary Medicine
Date of service: 01/05/2026
Reason for referral: productive cough and blood-streaked sputum after pneumonia

HPI: 33-year-old woman with chronic hypertension and a right attic cholesteatoma treated surgically last March. She describes a cough that has produced sputum every day for the better part of a year: copious, thick, yellow-green and foul, heaviest on waking. Now and then there are streaks of blood. She is tired, short of breath with exertion, and has lost weight over the last several months without trying. She had a right lower lobe pneumonia in November, treated with doxycycline by her PCP, two weeks after coming home from a two-month rural volunteer placement abroad. She works with toddlers in a busy daycare. She has never had asthma, allergies or any earlier lung problem.

Meds: labetalol 200 mg twice daily; prenatal vitamin daily. NKDA.
Smoking: about 5 pack-years, stopped at 26. No alcohol.
Family history: hypertension in both parents.
Quantiferon negative last month (PCP).

Exam: vital signs normal; weight 64.8 kg. Coarse crackles over the right lung base. Digital clubbing. No wheeze. Heart regular. No lymphadenopathy.

Chest X-ray today: tram-track and ring opacities at the right base; no consolidation, cavity or mass.

Assessment: Bronchiectasis, right base, with a current exacerbation (increased purulent sputum, hemoptysis streaking). Travel history makes it important to exclude mycobacterial infection.

Plan:
1. CT chest without contrast.
2. Sputum for routine culture and acid-fast smear and culture, three early-morning samples.
3. CBC with differential; quantitative immunoglobulins (IgG, IgA, IgM).
4. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily for 14 days.
5. Airway clearance: oscillating PEP device twice daily, taught today by our respiratory therapist.
6. Return in about 5 weeks with spirometry.

Thank you for asking me to see her.
Pulmonary Medicine

reports.text:
Technique: non-contrast CT of the chest with thin-section reconstructions.
Lungs: cylindrical bronchiectasis of the right lower lobe with bronchial wall thickening and mucus plugging. No cavitation. No mass or suspicious nodule. The remaining lobes are clear.
Airways: central airways patent.
Mediastinum: no lymphadenopathy. Heart normal size. No pericardial effusion.
Pleura: no effusion or pneumothorax.
Upper abdomen: unremarkable.
Bones: no aggressive lesion.
reports.conclusion: Cylindrical bronchiectasis of the right lower lobe with wall thickening and mucus plugging. No cavitation, mass or lymphadenopathy. Other lobes clear.

reports.text: Acceptable and repeatable efforts. FEV1 2.71 L (84% predicted). FVC 3.30 L (91% predicted). FEV1/FVC 0.82. Flow-volume loop normal in shape.

documents.title: Pulmonary Medicine follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside Pulmonary Medicine
Date of service: 02/11/2026

Ms. Lavoie finished the 14 days of amoxicillin-clavulanate. Sputum is down to a fraction of what it was, and there has been no blood since the middle of January. Her energy is better and her weight has held steady. She is doing the oscillating PEP device twice a day.

Results: CT chest - cylindrical bronchiectasis of the right lower lobe with wall thickening and mucus plugging, no cavitation or mass, other lobes clear. Sputum - normal flora; acid-fast smears negative on all three samples, cultures pending. CBC normal. IgG 1,040, IgA 212, IgM 118 mg/dL, all normal.

Spirometry today: FEV1 2.71 L (84%), FVC 3.30 L (91%), ratio 0.82 - no obstruction.

Assessment: Right lower lobe bronchiectasis, likely post-infectious; no other cause identified on this initial evaluation. Exacerbation resolved.

Plan: continue airway clearance daily, more often during colds. Please give her a pneumococcal vaccine. Call us early for increased sputum or blood. Return in 3 months.
Pulmonary Medicine

documents.title: Office Visit - follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after the lung workup.

Pulmonology letters (1/5, 2/11), CT chest and labs reviewed with her: right lower lobe bronchiectasis, felt to be post-infectious. TB evaluation negative throughout - Quantiferon negative in December, three AFB smears negative, AFB cultures final no growth on 2/20. Immunoglobulins normal. Spirometry normal.

She feels much better. A little sputum most mornings, cleared with the PEP device, which she does before work and at bedtime. No blood since mid-January. No fever. Weight 64.6, about where it was at pulmonology - no further loss.

Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: BP at goal. Vitals as charted. Lungs - a few crackles at the right base, no wheeze. Heart regular. R ear dry.

A/P
1. Bronchiectasis, RLL - on the problem list; pulmonology following, next visit May. Airway clearance daily. PCV20 today per pulmonology; flu and COVID done in December.
2. Weight loss - stable since January; recheck at next visit.
3. Cholesteatoma s/p R tympanomastoidectomy 3/2025 - ENT MRI due this spring.
4. Chronic HTN - controlled on labetalol 200 BID. Refills sent.
5. HM - Pap/HPV due this year.

RTC for physical in the summer.

reports.study: MRI internal auditory canals without contrast
reports.text:
Protocol: temporal bone imaging with non-echo-planar diffusion-weighted sequences, coronal T1 and T2. History: right canal-wall-up tympanomastoidectomy for cholesteatoma 03/2025.
No restricted diffusion in the right middle ear or mastoid. Postoperative changes of the right mastoid. Left temporal bone normal. Internal auditory canals and cerebellopontine angles normal. Visualized brain unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of residual or recurrent right cholesteatoma.

documents.title: Otolaryngology surveillance visit
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside Otolaryngology
Date of service: 04/08/2026

One year after right canal-wall-up tympanomastoidectomy for attic cholesteatoma. The ear has stayed dry. Exam: healed graft, no retraction, canal clean. Diffusion-weighted MRI 04/06: no restricted diffusion, no residual or recurrent disease.

Medications: labetalol, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Plan: yearly ear checks with us. Return sooner for drainage.
Otolaryngology

documents.title: Pulmonary Medicine follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside Pulmonary Medicine
Date of service: 05/20/2026

Three-month follow-up for right lower lobe bronchiectasis. Small amount of sputum in the mornings only, no blood, no exacerbation since January. Final acid-fast cultures were negative. Received pneumococcal vaccine in February.

Lungs: scattered crackles right base, otherwise clear. Oxygen saturation normal.

Plan: continue daily airway clearance with the PEP device. Early contact for any flare. Follow-up in 6 months.
Pulmonary Medicine
